description: Twenty-seven implicit behaviours recovered from src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs — magic numbers, magic strings, ordering dependencies, absent guards and emergent rates. None is documented in the code: the application contains zero comments, zero named constants and zero configuration values, so every threshold below is an inline literal. Each entry names the business rule (BR-*) it underpins in business-logic.json. Implicit behaviour IS business logic here: because the quality ceiling, the zero floor and the demand thresholds exist only as inline literals inside one 75-line method, a re-implementation that does not reproduce them exactly changes what the inn charges for its stock.

implicit_rules.name: magic_number_50_quality_ceiling
implicit_rules.description: The maximum quality of 50 is an inline literal repeated at four comparison sites with no named constant. Changing the cap means finding all four. It is expressed as a pre-increment guard (Quality < 50) rather than a post-increment clamp, which is what makes the no-overshoot property of BR-007 hold.

implicit_rules.name: magic_number_0_quality_floor
implicit_rules.description: The zero floor is an inline literal in two guards (Quality > 0) rather than a clamp. It is correct only because every decrement step happens to be exactly 1; the first multi-step degradation added to this code will undershoot it. The guard tests > 0 rather than != 0, so a negative seeded Quality is never corrected upward.

implicit_rules.name: magic_number_11_ten_day_demand_threshold
implicit_rules.description: The literal 11 encodes the documented '10 days or less' correctly only because it is evaluated before the SellIn decrement. Read in isolation the line looks like an off-by-one bug; it is not, and 'fixing' it to 10 would change pricing on the boundary day. This is the single most likely mis-transcription in any re-implementation.

implicit_rules.name: magic_number_6_five_day_demand_threshold
implicit_rules.description: The literal 6 encodes the documented '5 days or less', again only under the pre-decrement reading of SellIn. Same trap as IL-003, one tier lower.

implicit_rules.name: magic_number_80_legendary_quality_exists_only_as_seed_data
implicit_rules.description: The legendary quality of 80 appears exactly once in the application — in the seed list — and never in any rule. No code asserts it, defaults to it, or restores it, so the value survives only because nothing touches Sulfuras. It also sits 30 above the documented maximum of 50, making the two documented statements (README.md:23 and README.md:44-45) mutually inconsistent as written.

implicit_rules.name: degradation_rate_hardcoded_as_plus_or_minus_one
implicit_rules.description: There is no rate variable anywhere. Every adjustment is literally 1, and 'twice as fast' is expressed by executing a second separate ±1 statement in the same iteration rather than by multiplying a rate. That design is why the Conjured requirement (BR-MISSING-001) cannot be added as a simple multiplier.

implicit_rules.name: business_category_encoded_in_the_display_name
implicit_rules.description: The Item model has no category, type or SKU field. Three customer-facing display-name literals carry the entire business taxonomy across eight comparison sites, so the pricing rules are coupled to marketing copy: renaming the concert in the catalogue silently deletes its demand pricing.

implicit_rules.name: case_sensitive_whole_string_matching_only
implicit_rules.description: All name tests use C# operator == / != on string, which is ordinal, case-sensitive, culture-insensitive whole-string equality. There is no Trim, ToLower, StartsWith, Contains or comparer anywhere. 'aged brie', 'Aged Brie ' and 'AGED BRIE' are all standard goods.

implicit_rules.name: sell_in_read_before_and_after_its_own_decrement
implicit_rules.description: The highest-risk implicit behaviour in the application. Lines 59 and 67 read SellIn before the line 80 decrement; line 83 reads it after. One field therefore means two different things within one iteration, and the most natural cleanup a developer would make — hoisting the decrement — silently shifts outcomes on the boundary days SellIn 11, 6 and 0. No test detects it, because the only test asserts Assert.True(true).

implicit_rules.name: self_cancelling_expression_used_instead_of_zero_assignment
implicit_rules.description: Expired backstage passes are zeroed by `Items[i].Quality = Items[i].Quality - Items[i].Quality` rather than `= 0`. Any reader or tool searching for an assignment of literal zero will miss the rule entirely, and the expression reads like arithmetic rather than a business cliff.

implicit_rules.name: ceiling_re_tested_before_every_single_increment
implicit_rules.description: Because the Quality < 50 test is repeated before each of the three backstage increments rather than applied once at the end, a pass gaining +3 saturates at exactly 50 and can never reach 51 or 52. A re-implementation that computes a delta first and clamps afterwards produces the same result here, but only by coincidence of the numbers.

implicit_rules.name: concert_day_bonus_computed_then_discarded
implicit_rules.description: On the concert day a pass earns up to +3 at lines 55/63/71 and is then zeroed at line 99 in the same iteration. The work is wasted, and it repeats on every later day too: an already-worthless pass climbs to 3 and is reset to 0 each run. Net external behaviour is unaffected, but any re-implementation that logs, audits, publishes events or commits between phases would expose the non-zero intermediate as a real value.

implicit_rules.name: aged_brie_plus_two_per_day_is_emergent_not_stated
implicit_rules.description: Nothing in code or documentation says Aged Brie appreciates faster once expired. The +2 per day arises because the generic appreciation at line 55 and the expiry-branch appreciation at line 106 both fire in the same iteration. A reader checking the documentation alone would never predict it.

implicit_rules.name: legendary_sell_in_frozen_so_expiry_branch_is_unreachable
implicit_rules.description: Because Sulfuras is never decremented and is seeded at SellIn 0, its SellIn never becomes negative and it never enters the expiry branch. Its immutability is therefore doubly protected in practice — and one of those protections is invisible, resting on a seed value rather than on logic.

implicit_rules.name: legendary_guard_in_expiry_branch_is_data_dependent_dead_code
implicit_rules.description: The Sulfuras guard at line 91 is never evaluated for the seeded inventory (see IL-014), so it looks removable. It is not: a Sulfuras seeded with a negative SellIn reaches line 91 every single day, and that guard is the only thing preventing its quality from degrading. Whether the line is dead depends entirely on seed data — an invisible coupling between the rules engine and the item list.

implicit_rules.name: one_invocation_equals_one_business_day_with_no_clock
implicit_rules.description: No DateTime, timer, scheduler or date parameter exists anywhere in the application. 'A day' is defined purely as one call to UpdateQuality, and 'the sell-by date' is a countdown integer with no calendar anchor. Nothing can answer which real-world date an item expires on.

implicit_rules.name: repeat_execution_is_not_idempotent_and_is_unguarded
implicit_rules.description: Running the revaluation twice advances the inventory two days. There is no run-date record, no already-processed check and no lock, so in any variant of this system that did persist its results, a retry after a partial failure would double-apply a day of depreciation with no way to detect it.

implicit_rules.name: computed_results_are_never_emitted_anywhere
implicit_rules.description: The only console output in the entire application is the literal "OMGHAI!", printed BEFORE the calculation runs. No quality value is ever printed, returned, written or persisted, and the in-memory list dies with the process. The business output of the nightly revaluation is, today, unobservable.

implicit_rules.name: int_typing_admits_impossible_business_values
implicit_rules.description: SellIn and Quality are plain System.Int32 auto-properties with public setters and no range attribute or clamp, so Quality -100 or 9999 constructs cleanly and is never normalized. Every business constraint lives in the loop, not the type, so the model cannot be trusted by any future consumer.

implicit_rules.name: sell_in_decrements_without_a_floor_or_archival_path
implicit_rules.description: Only the sign of SellIn is ever tested, never its magnitude, so it falls indefinitely: -1, -2, -365. Nothing archives, writes off or removes a long-expired item, and no overflow guard exists. A downstream store using a narrower integer type would overflow where this code does not.

implicit_rules.name: null_name_never_throws_and_silently_prices_as_standard_goods
implicit_rules.description: C# string equality is null-safe, so a null Name does not raise at any of the eight comparison sites — it simply satisfies every 'is not a special item' test and falls through to the default depreciation path. The failure is silent: no exception, no log, no validation error. A default-constructed Item (Name null, SellIn 0, Quality 0) is processed as ordinary merchandise.

implicit_rules.name: rules_engine_is_unreachable_from_outside_the_assembly
implicit_rules.description: UpdateQuality is declared public but sits on the internal class Program and operates on the private instance field Items, so its effective accessibility is assembly-internal and it takes no parameters. The business rules cannot be invoked, tested or reused by any other assembly — which is precisely why the test project, though present, cannot exercise them.

implicit_rules.name: inventory_model_has_no_quantity_or_stock_count
implicit_rules.description: An 'inventory system' with no quantity field. Each Item instance represents exactly one unit, duplicates are not aggregated, and two identical goods with different quality must exist as two list entries. Nothing in the code can express 'twelve wheels of Aged Brie'.

implicit_rules.name: conjured_never_compared_despite_a_conjured_item_in_stock
implicit_rules.description: The string "Conjured" appears in the seed list (Program.cs:26) and in the business documentation (README.md:34) but nowhere in the rules. The item is silently priced as standard goods, so the documented doubled degradation is simply not happening. Recorded here as well as at BR-MISSING-001 because the absence is only visible by comparing three separate places.
implicit_rules.source: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:26; absent from src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:37-111; required by README.md:34

implicit_rules.name: no_audit_trail_of_any_valuation_change
implicit_rules.description: The revaluation mutates Quality at 13 sites and SellIn at 1 site with no before/after capture, no logging framework, no event and no versioning. Once a day is applied, the previous valuation is unrecoverable — there is no way to answer why an item is worth what it is worth.

implicit_rules.name: every_rule_in_this_catalog_is_untested
implicit_rules.description: The test project contains one method whose body is Assert.True(true) and holds no reference to GildedRose.Console, so behavioural coverage of the rules engine is exactly zero. This is what makes every implicit behaviour above dangerous rather than merely untidy: nothing would fail if a re-implementation changed any of them. A golden-master test over the seeded items is the prerequisite for touching this code.

implicit_rules.name: index_based_in_place_mutation_of_a_shared_list
implicit_rules.description: The loop re-reads Items[i] on roughly 25 separate lines instead of binding a local, and mutates the caller's list in place through public setters. Items.Count is re-evaluated every iteration, so concurrent modification is unsupported, and there is no lock, snapshot or copy — a rule change must be applied consistently across all ~25 access sites.
